official_sources.verified_fact: File.Replace replaces the destination with another file and can create a backup of the replaced file.
official_sources.limitation: The files must be accessible on a filesystem that supports the requested replacement semantics.

official_sources.verified_fact: ConvertFrom-Json converts JSON text into PowerShell objects; duplicate keys collapse to the last value.
official_sources.limitation: Duplicate keys are therefore not accepted as an integrity signal.

official_sources.verified_fact: ConvertTo-Json serializes PowerShell and .NET objects to JSON and supports a configurable nesting depth.
official_sources.limitation: Insufficient depth can truncate nested task contracts, so depth is set explicitly.

official_sources.verified_fact: A finally block runs when control leaves the try statement, including after terminating errors.
official_sources.limitation: External process termination or machine loss can still interrupt the host itself.

official_sources.verified_fact: Native programs report failure through non-zero exit codes tracked separately in LASTEXITCODE.
official_sources.limitation: A runner must preserve and act on the exit code instead of treating file publication as success.

official_sources.verified_fact: git update-ref supports transactional ref updates and aborts when a required ref cannot be locked.
official_sources.limitation: The slot reconciler updates queue files, not repository refs; this source supports the fail-closed lock model.

official_sources.verified_fact: Git worktree documentation recommends ref-aware commands rather than directly modifying internal ref files.
official_sources.limitation: The shared runner still must keep each task in a clean isolated worktree.

official_sources.verified_fact: File.Move moves a file to a new location and fails when a destination already exists on .NET Framework.
official_sources.limitation: Existing destinations use File.Replace; new destinations use Move to avoid partial JSON exposure.
